evidence: Hays — UT Plant Resources Center Flora of Purola Preserve, N. Hays County explicitly records Tripsacum dactyloides.
Travis — the Balcones Canyonlands Preserve plant list for Travis County explicitly includes eastern gamagrass (Tripsacum dactyloides).
Williamson — UT Plant Resources Center Vascular Plants of Williamson County provides a detailed field treatment of Tripsacum dactyloides.
target_zone_range.guardrail: No county occurrence inferred from statewide or ecoregion distribution alone.

morphology.look_here_first: Look at the flowering spike before anything else: a thick corn-relative spike has male spikelets on the upper portion and hard bead-like female spikelets below, all rising from a huge broad-leaved rhizomatous clump.
diagnostic_traits: robust warm-season perennial bunchgrass from thick creeping rhizomes
very broad straplike leaves, often strongly V-folded from a prominent midrib
inflorescence commonly one to three thick finger-like spikes
monoecious within the same spike: staminate spikelets above, pistillate spikelets below
female spikelets embedded in thick hard joints that break apart like beads
male spikelets paired and fitting into hollows along the upper rachis
solid culms and very dense coarse clump distinguish it from most local tallgrasses

confusers.separator: Big bluestem has several slender digitate 'turkey-foot' racemes and narrow typical grass spikelets; eastern gamagrass has a much thicker jointed corn-like spike with female bead-like joints below and male spikelets above.
Indiangrass produces a loose golden-bronze panicle of awned spikelets; eastern gamagrass has thick unbranched/few-branched jointed spikes and much broader coarse leaves.
